content: 1. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day when co-administered with clarithromycin, as clarithromycin can alter its metabolism. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Clarithromycin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but therapy should still be monitored closely. 3. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of etoposide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Etravirine increases the level or effect of omeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 5. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of eucalyptus by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 6. Co-administration of ezogabine and clarithromycin can increase the toxicity of either drug by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor the QT interval closely, especially when ezogabine is titrated to 1200 mg/day. 7. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 8. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of felodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Omeprazole decreases the level or effect of ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 10. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of omeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 11. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of finasteride by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 12. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of finerenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 13. Clarithromycin and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor therapy closely. 14. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of flibanserin by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Fluconazole increases the level or effect of omeprazole by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fludrocortisone by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Clarithromycin and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor therapy closely. 18. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of flurazepam by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 19. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fluticasone furoate and fluticasone inhaled by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Fluvoxamine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor therapy closely. 21. Omeprazole decreases the level or effect of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 22. Clarithromycin and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor therapy closely. 23. Fosphenytoin decreases the level or effect of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fostamatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib’s major active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction. 25. Omeprazole decreases levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration of gefitinib with proton pump inhibitors if possible. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Clarithromycin increases levels of gefitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Monitor therapy closely. 27. Clarithromycin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Iloperidone increases levels of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of gentamicin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Gepirone and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor therapy closely. 31. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 32. Clarithromycin increases levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by plasma protein binding competition. This increases the risk of hypoglycemia. Use caution and monitor therapy. 33. Goserelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor therapy. 34. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of guanfacine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 35. Histrelin increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of hydrocodone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Monitor therapy closely. 37. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of hydrocortisone by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 38. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor therapy. 39. Clarithromycin decreases the level or effect of ifosfamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. Monitor therapy closely. 40. Clarithromycin and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases levels of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 41. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of imatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 42. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of imipramine by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 43. Clarithromycin increases levels of inhaled indacaterol by modulating both P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor therapy. 44. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of indinavir by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 45. Omeprazole decreases the level or effect of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 46. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 47. Isoniazid increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy closely. 48. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of isradipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor therapy. 49. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of istradefylline by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Use caution and monitor therapy. 50. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of itraconazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 51. Omeprazole decreases levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases. Proton pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Use caution and monitor therapy. 52. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of ivacaftor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce ivacaftor dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product labeling for precise dosage modification. 53. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of ivermectin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. 54. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of ketoconazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 55. Clarithromycin increases levels of lacosamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider decreasing lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. 56. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of lansoprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 57. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of lapatinib by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor therapy closely. 58. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of lemborexant by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended if co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modification. 59. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor therapy. 60. Clarithromycin and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. Use caution and monitor therapy. 61. Clarithromycin increases levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Letermovir increases levels of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy and adjust doses as necessary. 62. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor therapy. 63. Omeprazole increases levels of lomitapide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. Use caution and monitor therapy. 64. Clarithromycin and levalbuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 65. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of levamlodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors results in increased systemic exposure to levamlodipine. Monitor therapy closely.
